summary.text: Franco Guardiani is One Nation's candidate for Preston at the 2026 Victorian election. He has an MBA from RMIT University and previously ran his family's concreting business. He has twice contested Batman, the federal seat that overlapped Preston, standing for the Palmer United Party in 2013 and as an independent in 2016.

summary.text: Hamza Al Katranji is the Liberal candidate for Preston at the 2026 Victorian election. His medical career, spanning surgery, health informatics and executive roles, has taken him to Saudi Arabia, New Zealand and Australia, including eight years in Victoria's public hospitals. He trained in medicine at Alexandria University in Egypt, went on to postgraduate study at the University of Melbourne, Harvard Medical School and Swansea University in Wales, and is secretary of the Australian Syrian Alliance.

occupation.text: Healthcare professional (surgeon, informatics specialist and executive)

priorities.text: Community safety, including the party's plan for more police and protective services officers and tougher sentencing
Easing cost-of-living pressure on households
Supporting local businesses
Quality healthcare

summary.text: Loki Sangarya is the Greens candidate for Preston at the 2026 Victorian election. He lives in Reservoir and works as an engineer and policy researcher, and is a union member. He stood for the Greens in the federal seat of Scullin in 2025, winning 9.4 per cent of first preferences.

priorities.text: I believe government decisions should be based on evidence, not vested interests.
Cheaper housing for renters and home owners, and secure tenancies
Keeping Preston Market in public ownership

summary.text: Nathan Lambert has been the Labor MP for Preston since 2022, having won preselection over the sitting member Robin Scott. He was a Victorian public servant before Parliament, working in energy, forestry and climate change. He is Parliamentary Secretary for Children and for Climate Action and an Acting Speaker, and is recontesting Preston in 2026.

prior_roles.organisation: Department of Jobs, Precincts and Regions

summary.text: Serena Ashmore is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Preston at the 2026 Victorian election. She has lived in Reservoir for about seven years, works in mental health and describes herself as an activist and union member. She says she has campaigned for Palestine, against Australian weapons manufacturing and military exports, and against racism and the far right.

priorities.text: We must put people before profit.
Serious action on rents and the housing crisis
Properly funded public services, with childcare, healthcare and aged care run as public services
Bringing Preston Market into public ownership
Upgrades to local facilities such as the Reservoir Leisure Centre

summary.text: William Fowles, known as Will Fowles, has been the member for Ringwood since 2022 and before that held Burwood from 2018, both won for Labor. He left the Labor caucus in August 2023 and the party itself in August 2024, and has since sat as an independent. He did not recontest Ringwood and is instead standing as an independent for Preston at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. Before entering Parliament he worked as a strategic communications consultant and ran a funds management business.

legal_and_integrity.text: Questioned by ACT Policing after he kicked in the door of a Canberra hotel room; he said he had been trying to reach medication locked inside and apologised.
legal_and_integrity.outcome: No charges were laid; he took a leave of absence for his health.

legal_and_integrity.text: Left Labor's parliamentary party when the then premier, Daniel Andrews, asked him to, after an allegation that he had assaulted a government employee; police investigated.
legal_and_integrity.outcome: Police decided in January 2024 not to lay charges; he was not readmitted to the caucus and left the Labor Party in August 2024.

summary.text: Zheng Chin is standing as an independent for Preston at the 2026 Victorian election. Trained in urban planning, he holds a doctorate from Monash University and has worked with the community campaign to save Preston Market, which he used as a case study in his research. He backed Gaetano Greco's independent campaign in Preston in 2022, and later lost a Darebin City Council race in Central Ward to Labor's candidate after preferences.

prior_roles.organisation: Save the Preston Market action group

previous_candidacies.note: His own site and Wikipedia's results give 2024 (Darebin's general council election); the ABC says 2025.

priorities.text: Put Preston Market in public hands
Suitable development along High Street, with money for parks, playgrounds and social services
Free and frequent public transport
Funding to redevelop the Reservoir Leisure Centre
Extending the tram line along Gilbert Road
